newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian police turn to medium in Dutroux case.
newsitem.headline: Belgian police turn to medium in Dutroux case.

text.p: Belgian police investigating the country's child sex, kidnap and murder case in which at least four girls have died, have turned to a French medium in a last-ditch effort to find clues.

"We cannot neglect even the slightest lead within the framework of our investigation. We know this means is unusual, but it has proven its worth (in the past)," spokesman Guy Soumoy of the Charleroi special branch told Reuters.

He did not give the name of the French parapsychologist, who was expected to begin work on Wednesday using information from parents of missing children who are suspected of having fallen into the hands of a gang which killed the four girls.
The man would search the site of a disused coal mine in Jumet near Charleroi, central Belgium, where police suspect Marc Dutroux, a convicted child rapist, has hidden the bodies of other children.

"This is the last approach open to us," Soumoy said. Scientific research of the Jumet site by Liege and Leuven university staff with sonar-type equipment to detect underground cavities had yielded nothing.
After Dutroux's arrest in August following a tip-off, two sexually abused young girls were rescued from one of his houses and the bodies of four others found.
Dutroux has been charged with murder, and police are still looking for at least six other missing chilrden.
